question: Which of the following is NOT an example of transfer payments given by the government to the households?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Interest of National debt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Transfer Payments** are defined as payments made by the **government** to individuals or **households** for which no current goods or services are rendered in return. These are **unilateral** or one-way transactions that do not contribute to the current flow of production.
 
• **Pensions**: Specifically, old-age pensions or social security payments are classic examples of **transfer payments**. They are provided to support elderly citizens without any expectation of current productive work or service. ***Hence, this is an example of a transfer payment.***
 
• **Scholarships**: These are financial aids provided by the **government** or institutions to students to assist with their education. Since the student does not provide a service or good to the **government** in exchange for this money, it is considered a **transfer payment**. ***Hence, this is an example of a transfer payment.***
